\[
H(R) = \left[\max_{R} Y - \min_{R} Y \le T\right],
\qquad
T = 30
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(H(R)\): Whether region R is uniform
- \(Y\): The luma in pixel levels
- \(T\): The threshold

The predicate H says whether a region R is uniform: its luma Y spans at most the threshold T. This predicate is our choice. Horowitz and Pavlidis allow any test of uniformity. The split starts with the whole image and cuts every block that fails into four quarters, down to the smallest block. The quadtree then over-segments, since a uniform area cut by the grid stays in many blocks. The merge joins two neighboring regions when their union still passes the test. Here the pairs with the closest mean brightness are tried first, which is also our choice, and a merged region is tested again with its new neighbors.
